text:
Maria: Ran a 30m nsys trace against the new batching heuristic on a realistic request mix (seq=512/2048 with KV cache warm). Wanted a quick sanity triage of hotspots.
Rahul: nice, any high level numbers? latency regressions visible in logs?
Maria: tail p90 tokens/sec dipped ~12% for small bursts. p99 tail increased ~70ms. No errors, just higher GPU time. Perf trace attached (perfetto link): https://perfetto.local/trace/2815
perf-bot: nsys aggregate summary (auto): top kernels by total GPU time -> attention_kv_gemm: 46.9% | softmax_fwd: 11.8% | kv_load_prefetch: 8.6% | gelu_fwd: 6.9% | ln_fwd: 3.2% | misc small kernels: 22.6%
Ben: attention_kv_gemm that high smells like fewer KV cache hits or poor kernel selection (fp16->int8 path mismatch?). Did you capture per-kernel launch size distribution?
Maria: yes, see snippet from nsys CLI (trimmed):
```
Kernel                          Calls   Total Time (ms)  Avg(ms)  %GPU
attention_kv_gemm              4,321   11234.5           2.60    46.9
softmax_fwd                    6,780    2825.1           0.42    11.8
kv_load_prefetch               2,112     2056.4          0.97     8.6
gelu_fwd                       3,900     1650.1          0.42     6.9
```
Sasha: kv_load_prefetch at ~0.97ms avg is suspicious — prefetching might be causing warp divergence and blocking other warps. Perfetto shows long gaps where SM occupancy drops right after prefetch kernels.
Rahul: occupancy numbers? SM util? warp stalls?
Maria: per-sm summary (perf-bot flags): average SM utilization ~38%, occupancy ~0.46, warp efficiency ~72%. Memory pipe utilization spikes during kv_load_prefetch.
Ben: 38% SM util + big attention kernel time = kernel does heavy math but low occupancy. Could be launch config using small threadblocks for short sequences. We should check kernel selector path: are we falling back to the generic GEMM for some shapes?
Sasha: I grepped the trace for kernel names + attrs — a subset of attention calls are using tiled_gemm_32x8 (low occupancy) vs tiled_gemm_64x16 (higher occupancy). The selector chose the smaller tile when batch coalescing produced many uneven micro-batches.
Maria: here's the selector log (excerpt):
```
batch_window=12ms -> microbatch sizes: [1,2,1,1,3,1,...]
selector: shape=(B=3,S=512) -> choose tiled_gemm_32x8 (fallback for odd S)
```
Rahul: so heuristics creating uneven micro-batches + selector fallback -> more launches of small-kernel variant -> SM underutilized -> higher overall time. And kv prefetch adds memory stalls on top.
Ben: ranking-wise I think priority suspects: 1) attention_kv_gemm tile choice (largest time) 2) microbatch coalescing heuristic (creates bad shapes) 3) kv_load_prefetch divergence 4) softmax kernel (maybe bank conflicts on S=512)
Sasha: agree. Small reproducible experiment: force selector to prefer 64x16 tile for S>=256 and rerun for 5m to see delta. Also try disabling prefetch to isolate memory stalls.
Maria: I ran a quick A/B yesterday: forcing 64x16 reduced attention_kv_gemm total time by ~18% and p99 dropped ~40ms. Disabling prefetch reduced memory pipe util spikes but increased KV read latency — overall effect on tokens/sec was neutral; combined change might be additive.
perf-bot: note: there is a perf regression alert linked -> PR #4892 changed microbatch coalescer (rolled out 3 days ago). Baseline traces pre-PR show attention_kv_gemm ~34% (vs 46.9% now).
Rahul: ok that points at coalescer change as root cause. Next steps: (1) revert coalescer patch in staging and run nsys 10m load (owner: @Maria) (2) add a selector override experiment to force 64x16 on staging (owner: @Ben) (3) instrument kv prefetch to record divergence counters per-SM (owner: @Sasha)
Ben: I'll add a flag for selector override. Also let's add an eviction profiler to ensure KV cache isn't thrashing causing additional load.
Sasha: adding perfetto capture points and sm counters. Will also dump `nvtx` ranges for microbatch boundaries to correlate.
Maria: created tickets: INF-1122 revert-coalescer, INF-1123 selector-experiment, INF-1124 kv-prefetch-counters. Kicking off staging runs now.
Rahul: great. Can we get an ordered hotspot ranking note for the incident postmortem? Put attention_kv_gemm first with fact-backed delta numbers and link to traces.
Maria: will draft the blameless notes once the staging traces finish. Quick ask: ping me if anyone sees other obvious regressions while the runs are in flight.
Ben: :thumbsup:
Sasha: :eyes:
